minutes.headline: Zoning Board granted three special permits: a front porch, a second-story addition, and an orthodontic office.
minutes.summary: The board heard three special permit hearings. It granted relief for a front porch at 189 Howard Street, a second-story addition at 617 Reservoir Road, and a use permit for an orthodontics office at 119 Massachusetts Avenue. The meeting opened with a town official describing new legal office hours for boards.

public_comment.topic: A Howard Street neighbor said there was never a porch on the front of the house; discussion of the 2004 permit for the concrete slab.

votes.motion: Grant the special permit for relief from the front setback for a porch roof at 189 Howard Street.

Grant the special permit for a second-story addition at 617 Reservoir Road, with a finding under section 7.4.1 that it is not substantially more detrimental than the existing non-conforming structure.
Grant the special permit under section 4.6.3.1.F for an orthodontics office at 119 Massachusetts Avenue.

decisions.decision: Porch special permit granted subject to compliance with all applicable regulations, periodic review, filing with the town clerk and recording at the Registry of Deeds; lapses in two years.
Reservoir Road special permit granted with the same standard conditions.
Massachusetts Avenue special permit granted with the same standard conditions.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals granted a special permit for relief from the front setback for a porch roof at 189 Howard Street; the count was not audible.
The board granted a special permit for a second-story addition at 617 Reservoir Road, with a finding that it is not substantially more detrimental than the existing non-conforming structure.
The board granted a use special permit for an orthodontics office at 119 Massachusetts Avenue under section 4.6.3.1.F.
Each permit carries standard conditions: compliance with regulations, periodic review, filing with the town clerk, recording at the Registry of Deeds, and lapse after two years.
A Howard Street neighbor said there had never been a porch on the front of the house, and the 2004 permit for the concrete slab was discussed.

why_it_matters: These permits change what may be built or operated at three specific properties, so neighbors of each address are the residents most directly affected.
A special permit lapses after two years if unused, and it must be recorded at the Registry of Deeds, so the approval stays on the property's record.
watch_next: Filing of each decision with the town clerk and recording at the Registry of Deeds, which the conditions require.
